extracted.intended_audience: Doctoral students (PhD candidates) considering applying to the DOE Office of Science Graduate Student Research (SCGSR) program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and program requirements for applying to the DOE Office of Science Graduate Student Research (SCGSR) supplemental award to conduct part of PhD thesis research at a DOE National Laboratory in collaboration with a DOE scientist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility — citizenship/residency
rubrics_metrics.description: The SCGSR program provides supplemental funds for U.S. graduate awardees (U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents are eligible; applicants should verify eligibility before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility — graduate/PhD status
rubrics_metrics.description: The program supports graduate awardees to conduct part of their PhD thesis research at a host DOE laboratory/facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be PhD students (proof of PhD candidacy is required as an application component). Confirm your PhD candidacy status and include required documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required collaboration with a DOE National Laboratory scientist
rubrics_metrics.description: Your application will require collaboration with a DOE National Laboratory scientist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must identify and secure a collaborating DOE National Laboratory scientist (collaborating scientists may be from any of the participating DOE National Laboratories and User Facilities). If needed, consult the running list of scientists ready to collaborate or contact program staff for help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with PhD thesis advisor
rubrics_metrics.description: Your application will require coordination with your PhD thesis advisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your thesis advisor is informed and supports the proposed SCGSR project and timeline; obtain any required letters or approvals from the advisor per application instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application components (transcripts, proof of candidacy, letters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application components include transcripts, proof of PhD candidacy, and letters of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closely review the application requirements, video guides, and FAQ to compile all required components. Obtain and include official transcripts, documentation of PhD candidacy, and necessary letters of support (e.g., from thesis advisor and collaborating scientist) as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with SCGSR priority research areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications should reference the program's priority research areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the published priority research areas and design the proposed research to align with those areas; the program points applicants to priority areas as part of the application requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are evaluated according to the program's merit review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must review the merit review criteria provided by the program. Although the page does not enumerate them in full here, applicants are instructed to review those criteria to prepare a competitive and compelling application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project purpose — advance PhD thesis research
rubrics_metrics.description: The award provides supplemental funds for awardees to conduct part of their PhD thesis research at a host DOE laboratory/facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should clearly describe how the project advances the applicant's PhD thesis research, demonstrating added value from access to DOE lab expertise and facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution eligibility — participating DOE labs and user facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborating DOE National Laboratory scientists may be from any of the participating DOE National Laboratories and User Facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the proposed host laboratory or user facility is a participating DOE site; verify the collaborating scientist's affiliation is with an eligible participating institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award period duration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The award period for the proposed research project may range from 3 to 12 consecutive months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose a continuous award period between 3 and 12 months that matches your research needs and PhD timeline; use key dates to determine the appropriate timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timeliness and key dates
rubrics_metrics.description: As you prepare to apply, check out the key dates to determine the time frame that best matches your research needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify application deadlines, award start/end dates, and other timeline constraints to ensure proposed research period and institutional approvals are feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should review participant obligations associated with the SCGSR award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the participant obligations resources to understand reporting, conduct, and program requirements that accompany the award and factor these into planning and advisor discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of DOE expertise, facilities, and instrumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees conduct research while collaborating with world-class scientists and using state-of-the-art facilities and cutting-edge scientific instrumentation available at DOE National Laboratories and User Facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how access to DOE-specific expertise, facilities, or instrumentation is essential to completing the proposed tasks and advancing the thesis; explain the unique value the host lab provides over the applicant's home institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended preparation — attend application assistance workshop
rubrics_metrics.description: Sign up for SCGSR 'how to apply' workshops to answer questions and help empower you during the application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend available application assistance workshops and review video guides and FAQs to improve application completeness and competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional benefit — short international research visit possibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees may have the opportunity for conducting a short international research visit to a prestigious institution abroad such as CERN or RIKEN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a potential opportunity/benefit rather than a requirement; include plans or contingencies only if applicable and supported by your host/collaborator.
